explanation: Exchanging business cards is a standard and expected part of business introductions in Indonesia, typically done after the initial handshake and greetings. Cards are treated as a representation of the person and their company, so they must be presented and received with both hands and handled with visible respect. Failing to do so—such as tossing a card with one hand—can cause real offense.
local_tip: Present and receive cards with both hands, give a slight bow, and take a moment to read the card with genuine interest before placing it respectfully on the table or in a card case—never in a back pocket.

also_check.note: Card exchange (meishi) is highly ritualized; present with both hands, bow, and read carefully—casual handling is disrespectful.
Exchange with both hands and receive with both hands; study the card briefly before putting it away.
Casual one-handed exchange is normal; elaborate two-handed rituals may seem overly formal but are not offensive.
